sources.title: The Latest Injury Updates Impacting Fantasy Football Wide Receivers
sources.notes: Published Sept. 1, 2026. User supplied the Yahoo-syndicated version; the canonical Athlon article was used for reliable ingestion. Injury, practice and Week 1 status are time-sensitive.

sources.title: The Latest Injury Updates Impacting Fantasy Football Running Backs
sources.notes: Published Aug. 27, 2026. Injury, practice, recovery and Week 1 status are time-sensitive.

sources.title: Josh Jacobs out indefinitely: How Fantasy Football rankings, drafts should approach Packers' RBs, passing game
sources.notes: Published Aug. 31, 2026. Legal/league availability status and resulting role projections are highly time-sensitive; allegations and possible discipline are not treated as adjudicated facts.

facts.summary: Nacua returned after nearly three weeks away but had not completed an unrestricted practice because of psoas soreness as of Sept. 1; the Rams still expected him to play Week 1.

outlook.summary: Athlon sees no major-injury signal but recommends monitoring full-practice participation before treating his opening-week workload as completely normal.

facts.summary: Chase was recovering from a left-knee hyperextension and was expected to be limited in practice, while Cincinnati expected him to be ready for Week 1.

outlook.summary: Athlon does not recommend changing Chase's first-round fantasy value unless his knee responds poorly as activity increases.

facts.summary: Nabers said he felt good but did not commit to Week 1, and he avoided Reserve/PUP; he had no preseason action.

outlook.summary: Athlon considers an early snap limit possible even if Nabers is cleared for the opener.

facts.summary: Egbuka had not participated in team work since an Aug. 12 toe sprain and missed practice again Sept. 1, though Tampa Bay remained optimistic about Week 1.

outlook.summary: The shrinking preparation window creates legitimate early-season utility risk.

facts.summary: Burden returned to the field after a groin issue, but Chicago had not confirmed full team-drill participation as of Sept. 1.

outlook.summary: Athlon views the missed camp time as a possible drag on Burden's early-season emergence.

facts.summary: Pierce was activated from Active/PUP and practicing, but his ankle rehab cost him the offseason program and most of camp; Indianapolis had not confirmed an unrestricted workload.

outlook.summary: Athlon says a possible early snap limit belongs in Pierce's fantasy evaluation.

facts.summary: Flowers had missed recent practices with a lower-body issue, but Baltimore expected him to resume unrestricted work and be available for Week 1.

outlook.summary: Athlon sees no current reason for a meaningful fantasy downgrade.

facts.summary: Higgins was expected to be limited by a bruised heel, which Cincinnati described as minor, with Week 1 availability expected.

outlook.summary: Athlon keeps Higgins at normal WR2 value while recommending confirmation of unrestricted practice before the opener.

facts.summary: Evans was limited to side work by an adductor injury, with San Francisco hoping to return him to practice before the opener.

outlook.summary: The situation remains unresolved and should be monitored before drafting at full health value.

facts.summary: General stiffness kept Tate out of Sept. 1 practice, with Tennessee not identifying an affected area or indicating a lengthy absence.

outlook.summary: A small monitoring flag until the rookie returns to normal work.

facts.summary: Downs returned to practice Sept. 1 after a calf injury and Indianapolis had not indicated serious Week 1 concern.

outlook.summary: His return prevents a substantial fantasy downgrade unless a setback occurs.

facts.summary: Shakir had missed more than two weeks with an undisclosed issue and Buffalo had not provided a return timetable as of Sept. 1.

outlook.summary: Athlon says fantasy managers should not assume a normal Week 1 slot role until Shakir resumes team work.

facts.summary: New Orleans placed Tyson on injured reserve with a designation to return, guaranteeing at least a four-game absence; the source says the original recovery estimate still pointed toward later October.

outlook.summary: No early-season redraft utility; return timing remains uncertain beyond the minimum IR window.

facts.summary: McMillan remained sidelined by a prolonged knee problem with no firm return date as of Sept. 1.

outlook.summary: Athlon sees too little early-season clarity for standard redraft leagues, particularly with Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin ahead when healthy.

facts.summary: Higgins suffered a torn ACL during an Aug. 18 joint practice and will miss the entire 2026 season.

outlook.summary: No 2026 redraft value.

facts.summary: Coleman's right foot/toe sprain no longer required a walking boot and he was present at Sept. 1 practice.

outlook.summary: The recovery is progressing with time remaining before Week 1, but full participation is still the next checkpoint.

facts.summary: Houston placed Dell on injured reserve with a designation to return, guaranteeing at least four missed games; the source says a longer recovery remains plausible because of the severity of his knee injury.

outlook.summary: Early-season availability is absent and the actual return date may extend beyond the minimum IR window.

facts.summary: San Francisco placed Kirk on injured reserve with a designation to return, ruling him out for at least the first four games.

outlook.summary: Athlon recommends leaving Kirk outside standard redraft player pools for now.

facts.summary: Bell made his preseason debut less than 10 months after an ACL tear and finished without a reported setback, but missed nearly all of camp.

outlook.summary: Availability concern has eased, but Athlon considers an early offensive role unlikely and views him as a dynasty/deep-league watch-list player.

facts.summary: Hill remained unsigned and had not provided a return timetable after a major 2025 knee injury involving a dislocation, ACL tear and additional ligament damage.

outlook.summary: Athlon considers him unsuitable for standard 2026 redraft leagues at this time.

facts.summary: Pearsall underwent season-ending surgery after swelling developed in the knee that sustained a PCL injury in 2025.

outlook.summary: No 2026 redraft value.

facts.summary: Brazzell suffered a left LCL injury, was moved to injured reserve and will miss the 2026 season.

outlook.summary: No 2026 redraft value; the injury also creates additional opportunity for Carolina's remaining receivers.

facts.summary: Love had no on-field work during the Aug. 24 practice week after a high-ankle sprain; Arizona still hoped for a Week 1 return, with Tyler Allgeier positioned to lead if Love sits.

outlook.summary: Athlon considers a normal opening-week workload difficult to project and calls the risk substantial at Love's draft cost.

facts.summary: Jeanty suffered a right ankle sprain Aug. 23; the Raiders believed it was a low rather than high sprain and did not expect a lengthy absence, but Week 1 remained uncertain.

outlook.summary: Athlon retains Jeanty's early-round value but says drafting before another health update carries added risk.

facts.summary: Henderson avoided a serious right-ankle injury and was expected to be available for Week 1, though he missed the preseason finale.

outlook.summary: No substantial draft downgrade, but Athlon notes Stevenson could open the season with the larger backfield share.

facts.summary: Walker had ankle swelling that Kansas City attributed to cleat irritation and was expected to be fine, with a return to full practice the remaining checkpoint.

outlook.summary: Athlon does not recommend changing his draft cost unless swelling persists into game-week preparation.

facts.summary: Croskey-Merritt was limited to side work after an unspecified lower-body injury, and Washington had not provided a return date.

outlook.summary: He retains late-round appeal, but Athlon considers the uncertain Week 1 outlook materially riskier than earlier in camp.

facts.summary: Hall was doing side-field agility work after a right-groin strain but had not returned to team drills; the Jets expected him for Week 1.

outlook.summary: Expected Week 1 availability limits the downgrade, but full-team clearance remains an important checkpoint.

facts.summary: Hubbard remained out of contact work while rehabbing a hamstring, though Carolina said he was on schedule for Week 1; Jonathon Brooks had strengthened his committee case.

outlook.summary: Athlon recommends drafting Hubbard with a shared workload in mind even if cleared for the opener.

facts.summary: White had returned to individual work after a hamstring tweak but had not resumed full-speed team periods; Week 1 still appeared realistic.

outlook.summary: Health uncertainty remains, but Athlon says White's receiving ability preserves PPR flex appeal.

facts.summary: Kamara was recovering from an MCL sprain with a four-to-six-week timetable, and New Orleans added Zamir White while he recovered.

outlook.summary: Athlon considers Week 1 in serious doubt and views the added depth plus likely committee as meaningful draft risk.

facts.summary: Monangai hyperextended his right knee and was expected to miss multiple weeks, though he avoided a more serious injury requiring surgery.

outlook.summary: The multi-week timetable creates meaningful opening-week uncertainty.

facts.summary: Charbonnet remained on Active/PUP while recovering from January ACL injury and February surgery, with Seattle not establishing a return timetable.

outlook.summary: Athlon considers an extended absence realistic and frames him primarily as an injury stash for leagues with enough bench or IR space.

facts.summary: Conner had not reached 11-on-11 work during recovery from foot surgery, and Arizona said it was too early to know whether he would play Week 1; Tyler Allgeier was the healthy top-group back at the time.

outlook.summary: Opening-week availability and workload are uncertain, increasing Allgeier's contingent value.

facts.summary: Detroit said Pacheco's prior knee concern had eased but a new back issue had no clear return timetable, leaving Week 1 uncertain.

outlook.summary: Athlon finds his limited ceiling difficult to justify in standard drafts until he returns to practice.

facts.summary: Mitchell missed practice after what Mike McDaniel called a mild setback, interrupting a push for the No. 2 role behind Omarion Hampton.

outlook.summary: His late-round standalone appeal remains, but the absence weakens the immediate role case and would boost Kimani Vidal if it persists.

facts.summary: Guerendo remained on Active/PUP beyond the initial expected return window, with a Reserve/PUP move still capable of forcing at least a four-game absence.

outlook.summary: The delayed return and healthier competition reduce his early path to playing time behind Christian McCaffrey.

facts.summary: Benson was waived with an injury designation after his surgically repaired knee failed to tolerate a return, then reverted to injured reserve.

outlook.summary: Athlon assigns no realistic 2026 Arizona redraft value.

facts.summary: Harris was handling live team drills without a reported setback less than 11 months after an Achilles tear, but remained in a crowded Giants backfield and still had to secure a role.

outlook.summary: The recovery is encouraging, but Athlon sees little redraft appeal without a clearer roster spot and workload.

facts.summary: Athlon cites a July report that Mixon told former teammates his playing career was over, while noting he had not filed retirement paperwork and had undergone another foot procedure.

outlook.summary: Athlon recommends keeping Mixon outside all 2026 redraft player pools.

facts.summary: CBS reports Jacobs was placed on the NFL commissioner's exempt list after being charged with battery and criminal damage to property; while on the list he cannot play or practice. The duration was unknown as of Aug. 31.

outlook.summary: CBS advises against drafting Jacobs with any reasonable expectation of near-term availability and treats a lengthy absence, including a season-long absence, as possible.

entries.notes: This is a current availability signal, not a judgment about the underlying allegations or eventual discipline.

facts.summary: CBS expects Lloyd and Christopher Brooks to handle Green Bay rushing work while Jacobs is unavailable and notes that Lloyd entered the season healthy after two injury-limited years.

outlook.summary: CBS moves Lloyd into RB3 draft territory with RB2 upside and expects his market price to rise into roughly the top-80, potentially top-60 range.

facts.summary: CBS expects Brooks to share rushing duties while Jacobs is unavailable and views him as the likely passing-down option.

outlook.summary: CBS considers Brooks a late PPR-format bench swing rather than a high-priority standard-league target.

facts.summary: Green Bay acquired Kaleb Johnson from Pittsburgh for a future sixth-round pick after Jacobs became unavailable.

outlook.summary: CBS views Johnson mainly as contingent depth behind Lloyd while Jacobs remains unavailable.

facts.summary: CBS says Green Bay has been approximately 55% pass in selected neutral situations with Jordan Love on the field and Jacobs off it, compared with an overall 50/50 pass-run split across the prior two seasons.

outlook.summary: CBS expects Jacobs' absence to create a small target-volume boost for Love and Green Bay pass catchers rather than a wholesale offensive transformation.
